Electrifying combine performance (4.30 forty, 42.5" vertical, 10'11" broad — top scores among WRs) but 2025 production at Oklahoma was modest at 57 catches/620 yards/4 TDs after injury-shortened 2024. Has injury history (soft tissue, concussion); Bleacher Report ranks him #11 WR post-combine.

Freakish athleticism for his size (4.31 forty — fastest ever by a 6'1"+ player at the combine, 42" vertical) but only 32 catches for 478 yards and 6 TDs with 8.6% drop rate at Cincinnati in 2025. Raw, developmental big-body receiver; Day 3 projection despite the combine buzz.

Team leader at Baylor with 69 catches for 872 yards and 9 TDs in 2025; 2-time All-Big 12, physical possession receiver at 6'2"/220 lbs. Tankathon has him at #183 overall; projects as Day 3 pick with dense build but limited change-of-direction.

Led Missouri with 66 catches for 732 yards and 1 TD in 2025 after stints at Jackson State, Louisville, Mississippi State (74 rec/932 yds/6 TD in 2024), and Missouri; a prolific transfer portal journeyman with versatility. Projects as a slot/possession receiver with track record of 700+ yard seasons.

Led national champion Indiana with 69 catches for 937 yards and 13 TDs in 2025; Dane Brugler ranks him 22nd overall (The Athletic), Tankathon has him at #24. Physical slot receiver with exceptional YAC and hands; 24 career TDs and 1,798 career yards; rising first-round buzz.

qb_accuracy_context.qb_accuracy_note: #3 FBS accuracy (69.0% accurate, 16.3% uncatchable). Elite QB precision context — Cooper's 138.9 QBR when targeted partially reflects clean ball placement, not solely separation quality.
qb_accuracy_context.source: PFF 2025 FBS Most Accurate Passers (true attempts only, excluding throwaways/spikes)

evidence_summary: Six-year college career culminated with 50 catches for 557 yards and 7 TDs at Miami in 2025; career totals of 198 rec/2,996 yards/28 TDs. ESPN labeled him a 'Day 3 sleeper'; fluid route runner with natural ball-tracking ability but lacks top-end burst.

Impressive 54 catches for 846 yards (15.7 YPR) and 7 TDs at Texas Tech in 2025; 135 career catches for 2,031 yards and 16 TDs. Ran a 4.39 forty at 6'3"/206 lbs which is elite size/speed combination; projects as a Day 7 developmental outside receiver with an intriguing physical profile.

36 catches for 630 yards and 5 TDs at Notre Dame in 2025 with an elite 17.5 YPR; 9.98 RAS (top 2% ever) but 4.61 forty will be a concern for NFL evaluators. At 6'5"/218 lbs he's a massive red-zone target; pure raw upside prospect limited by below-average speed.

Led Kansas with 45 catches for 766 yards and 5 TDs in 2025 (17.0 YPR), earning 3rd-team All-Big 12 as receiver and 1st-team as kick returner; 1,237 all-purpose yards. Projects primarily as a Day 3 receiver/returner; not among the top-ranked WRs on most boards.

Only 7–10 receptions for 54–122 yards and 0 TDs in 2025 at LSU; career totals of 41 receptions across five years in college. His draft case rests almost entirely on all-star game appearance (Senior Bowl, Shrine Bowl, Hula Bowl, American Bowl — believed to be first player at all four), not production.

61 catches for 766 yards and 6 TDs at SMU in 2025 (career highs), including a 70-yard TD catch at Clemson; 3rd-team All-ACC. Transferred from TCU; ESPN Matt Miller ranks him 246th overall. Solid possession receiver but projected as a late-round or UDFA candidate.

First Georgia State player to cross 1,000 yards (71 rec/1,004 yds/6 TD in 2025); First Team All-Sun Belt and first Georgia State player on The Athletic's College Freaks List. Big (6'4") with 99th-percentile broad jump; Sun Belt level of competition is a caveat but athleticism is genuine.

60 catches for 635 yards and 2 TDs receiving at Louisville in 2025, but was a dominant return specialist (20.0 punt return average — 3rd nationally, two punt return TDs, 2nd-team All-American as returner). Dane Brugler (The Athletic) projects him as a priority UDFA; slot receiver with elite short-area quickness.

Set NDSU records with back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons (2024: 75 rec/1,071 yds/17 TD; 2025 comparable elite FCS numbers); 9.98 RAS — 7th highest in NFL Combine history. ESPN Matt Miller projects him at pick 96 overall; FCS production caveat but athleticism and production are both elite.

49 catches for 750 yards (15.3 YPR) and 4 TDs at USC in 2025; 77.6 overall PFF grade. Contested catch specialist who wins above the rim; Bleacher Report ranks him 21st among WRs; ESPN Scouts Inc. places him 91st overall. Route tree still developing but size/athletic combination is intriguing.

qb_accuracy_context.qb_accuracy_note: #34 FBS accuracy (61.5% accurate, 23.3% uncatchable). Same QB context as Lemon — production at 127.6 QBR when targeted despite elevated uncatchable rate.
qb_accuracy_context.source: PFF 2025 FBS Most Accurate Passers (true attempts only, excluding throwaways/spikes)

evidence_summary: Led Kentucky with 53 catches for 540 yards and 3 TDs in 2025 (10.2 YPR); 42-inch vertical (3rd among all combine WRs) and 9.60 RAS show elite athleticism. However, he ran a narrow route tree built around screens and hitches with an average depth of target under 4 yards. Primarily Day 3/UDFA range.

Elite college production in 2025 with 72 catches for 1,190 yards (16.5 YPR) and 10 TDs at TCU; AP and Sporting News All-American, led the Big 12 in receiving yards. Record game vs. SMU (254 yds/3 TDs). Did not perform on-field drills at the combine; projects as WR24 at #154 overall per NFLDraftBuzz.

39 catches for 588 yards and 3 TDs at Michigan in 2025 starting all 13 games; began career as a QB at Indiana before converting. Measured 6'5" and 215 lbs with huge hands (10.25"). Projects as a developmental UDFA/late-round pick; PFF ranks him 228th among WRs in 2025.

46 catches for 658 yards and 2 TDs at Georgia Tech in 2025; career totals of 140 rec/2,200 yds/16 TDs across Memphis, FIU, and Georgia Tech. Elite speed (4.35 forty) for his size; ranked #176 overall per Tankathon. Best as a vertical deep threat/special teams contributor.

54 catches for 802 yards and 6 TDs at BYU in 2025; 8th all-time at BYU in receptions (170 career) and 7th in yards. Puka Nacua comparison but slower (4.64) and projects as Day 3 or UDFA per ESPN; wins with contested catches and contested body positioning rather than separation speed.

55 catches for 811 yards and 6 TDs at Ole Miss in 2025; transferred between Washington State, Oklahoma State, and Ole Miss. Heavily vertical route tree with recent development; showed 50+ catches and 800+ yards at multiple programs. Speed (4.36) is a genuine weapon but overall draft stock is Day 3/UDFA.
context_source: Grok/Sports-Reference verification (April 2026); multi-program Power-4 career confirmed

evidence_summary: Only 27 catches for 406 yards and 3 TDs at Florida in 2025 after transferring from Cal; was a breakout freshman at Cal in 2022 (65 rec/755 yds/7 TD — led all FBS freshmen). Long injury/transfer history has never let him build on his freshman season; high upside but low floor.

41 catches for 488 yards and 4 TDs at LSU in 2025; ran the second-fastest 40 (4.28) at the entire combine among all positions. Limited route tree and volume but elite speed; ESPN Matt Miller projects him at pick 268. Projects as a specialty/speed player.

57 catches for 705 yards and 6 TDs at Texas Tech in 2025; 100 career catches for 1,583 yards and 16 TDs across Miami (OH) and Texas Tech. Matt Miller projects him pick 181 (Detroit Lions, 5th round); Big 12 honorable mention with reliable hands but route tree needs refinement.

61 catches for 934 yards and 4 TDs at Ole Miss in 2025 (15.3 YPR) after transferring from Penn State; ranked 32nd nationally in receiving yards. Career totals of 132+ catches and 1,950+ yards across Penn State and Ole Miss. Functional route runner; Day 3 to UDFA range.

70 catches for 847 yards and 8 TDs at Incarnate Word in 2025; had elite 2024 season (1,290 yds/14 TD) at the FCS level earning Southland Offensive Player of the Year. FCS competition is a significant caveat; #7 FCS prospect per FCS Football Central. Projects as UDFA/late Day 3.

Only 20 catches for 151 yards as a receiver at Iowa in 2025, but a historic returner: 2x Jet Award winner (nation's best returner), 28.3 punt return average (#1 in NCAA), 4 return TDs (3 punt, 1 kick). His draft value is almost entirely return specialist based, not as a receiver.

26 catches for 358 yards and 1 TD in 8 games before suffering a fractured leg vs. Ole Miss in October 2025; returned for the College Football Playoff. Intriguing 6'5"/218 lb frame with strong contested-catch ability but injury and legal history flagged; Steelers Depot grades him 6.2 (Pure Backup).

Broke out as a first-time full starter in 2025 with 48 catches for 620 yards and 6 TDs at Utah, earning Mackey Award semifinalist nod. A one-year production sample on a single-season breakout, but clean hands and intermediate route feel boost his upside.

Blocking-first TE from Nebraska transfer who posted just 19 catches for 198 yards and 3 TDs in his final year at Texas A&M; ran a surprising 4.40 shuttle at the combine. Projects as a developmental run-blocker with limited receiving role.

Posted 37 catches for 411 yards and 4 TDs in 2025 at Alabama with advanced zone feel and smart route running; 118 career receptions across five seasons show steady production. Lacks prototypical TE size but projects as a functional rotational TE2.

Spent his Penn State career primarily as a blocking TE with just 14 catches for 169 yards in 2025; excelled in 3-cone and shuttle at the combine, showing agility. Projects as a blocking specialist with minimal receiving ceiling.

Posted 33 catches for 346 yards and 3 TDs in his first year at Texas (transfer from Cal) while earning Arch Manning's trust as a dependable underneath option. Good size and dual-role capability make him an appealing Day 3 prospect.

Explosive move TE from Wyoming who barely played football before college yet became an NFL prospect; hamstring injury in 2025 limited him to partial production across 80 career catches for 1,023 yards and 7 TDs. Rare burst and seam speed for the position; blocking is the clear limitation.

Michigan transfer to SMU who posted 31 catches for 436 yards and 4 TDs in 2025; standout combine with a 4.57 40 and 37-inch vertical demonstrating above-average athleticism. Senior Bowl performer rising on draft boards with upside as a receiving TE2.

First-team All-ACC in 2025 with 47 catches for 468 yards and 7 TDs, leading NC State with his red-zone presence; did not run the 40 at the combine due to a hamstring injury. Natural pass catcher with strong hands and zone feel but undersized frame raises NFL ceiling questions.

Blocking-first TE at Ohio State with just 15 catches for 168 yards and 2 TDs in 2025; used primarily to open holes in Ohio State's run-heavy sets. Limited receiving upside but respected as a technician in pass protection and short-area blocking.

Converted linebacker — played LB at Kansas State before transferring to Oklahoma, where he switched to TE in 2025 and produced 44 catches for 533 yards with All-SEC Third Team recognition; elite 4.52 40-dash for the position reflects LB athleticism. Extreme developmental upside with only one year of TE experience.

Blocking-and-receiving TE at Tennessee with 26 catches for 261 yards and 2 TDs in 2025; heavy NFL-ready frame at 6'5", 259 lbs but 4.90 40 time is a red flag for receiving role upside. Projects as a late-round blocking TE2/developmental prospect.

German-born, rare athletic specimen at 6'6" with a 4.61 40 and exceptional combine testing; only 24 catches for 248 yards in 2025 as Michigan's blocking TE in a run-heavy scheme. Elite developmental upside if he refines route running and receives more targets.

BOA 19 true freshman impact at Ball State (31.1 rec ypg, 91.0 PFF receiving grade). Led all FBS TEs in combined receptions 2024-2025 (168, tied Vandeross). Career: 237 rec / 2,236 yds / 24 TDs — leads all TE prospects since 2019 in routes, targets, receptions, and first downs. Slot YPRR 2.25 overall in 2025, 2.64 slot YPRR (3rd best P4 TE since 2014 behind Mark Andrews 2.94, Loveland 2.87). Career 61.3% contested catch rate (3rd all-time P4 history, min 25 contested targets; Warren 63.6, Joly 66.0). Zone YPRR > 3.00 in a single season + career contested catch > 50%: comp group = Mark Andrews, Brock Bowers, Trey McBride, Isaiah Likely. KEY CONCERN: career man YPRR 1.21 (34.7th pctile); zone YPRR 1.95 (72.7th pctile) — zone-scheme fit is actually POSITIVE for NFL translation vs man YPRR 1.95 — zone-heavy NFL is a genuine translation risk. 1D/RR 0.125 (7th among all WR/TEs last 2 seasons; Pitts/McBride/Bowers/Kincaid/Warren tier). Reception share 33.6% (2024) / 30.6% (2025) — comp tier: Harold Fannin, Tyler Warren, Trey McBride. 87.6 PFF receiving grade vs P4 (2nd in class behind Stowers 89.1). 1.86 YPRR vs P4 competition (3rd in class). KLP RAS 9.72 (size-adjusted elite; system ras_0_100 = 49.0 reflects speed-heavy formula, 4.71 40 / 54th pctile speed score). WEAKNESSES: zone YPRR 1.21, YAC 3.51/rec (bottom 3rd pctile despite 8.12 ADOT), 7.6% MTF rate, poor blocking (only 41% inline snaps, lacks leverage). Only 5% deep target share — short-intermediate floor role. NFL comp: Mike Gesicki. Day 3 draft projection. TEP premium target.
context_source: X research batch (April 2026): @ffdataroma, PFF, Scott Barrett, various FFX accounts; Sports-Reference cross-verification
ras_klp_note: SPORQ 70.2 (replaces system ras_0_100 49.0 which over-penalized 4.71 40 time); KLP RAS 9.72 size-adjusted

evidence_summary: Son of Super Bowl champion Russell Maryland, posted 27 catches for 322 yards and 2 TDs at SMU in 2025 with elite seam speed (4.51 40) and alignment versatility; finished career as SMU's all-time leader in TE receiving yards. Receiving instincts and athleticism are clear, but blocking and route refinement need work.

Five-year USC starter who posted 30 catches for 450 yards and 4 TDs in his final season; two prior ACL tears (high school and 2023 at USC) raise durability flags. Smooth route runner with good hands but testing data from the combine was not publicly available.

Starter on Indiana's undefeated 2025 regular season squad with 32 catches for 387 yards and 2 TDs plus a rushing score; reliable blocker and intermediate target for the Big Ten champion Hoosiers. Best suited as an H-back/move TE in creative schemes.

6'7" frame with 32 catches for 482 yards in 2025 at Notre Dame; missed nearly two full seasons recovering from double ACL tears early in his career. Legitimate injury history clouds his floor but his size-speed combination and length at the catch point project as a moldable Y-TE.

Late-blooming five-year TCU TE who finally broke out with 34 catches for 319 yards and 2 TDs in 2025 as the starter; did not run the 40 or perform drills at the combine. PFF ranks him 292nd overall; projects as a Day 3 depth/blocking TE.

49 catches for 545 yards and 2 TDs in 2025, leading ACC TEs in receiving yards; posted the best 3-cone (7.08) among all TEs at the combine and a 38.5-inch vertical that locked up Day 2 consideration. Old-school Y-TE with elite effort and blocking willingness; drop issues need to be cleaned up.

Ohio State transfer who posted 29 catches for 416 yards and 4 TDs in 2025 final year at Cincinnati; returned for senior season specifically to be the first TE taken in 2026. Excellent hands and zone feel, but did not perform combine drills; blocking development is his NFL key.

Unique background: started as a QB at Southeastern Louisiana, transferred to Oklahoma (2024, 42 catches) then LSU (2025, 24 catches for 252 yards and 2 TDs). Journey player with multi-position athleticism but limited TE production at power programs.

Two-time All-America TE at Baylor with 50 catches for 694 yards and 6 TDs in 2025, finishing 2nd nationally in TE receiving yards; hamstring pull forced him to shut down all combine testing. Three-time consensus All-American; contested-catch ability and vertical athleticism are elite but blocking needs major development.

39 catches for 635 yards and 5 TDs at Ole Miss in 2025 with a 16.3 YPC average that ranked among the nation's best for TEs; played through an undisclosed injury all season. Aligned all over the formation with big-play ability, though he skipped combine drills and blocking is a notable weakness.

D2 transfer (Shepherd → North Texas) with one FBS season: 44 rec/769 yds/6 TD in 2025. Elite efficiency metrics — QBR when targeted 160.4 (2nd in class), man YPRR 3.01, 1D rate 12.0%, avoided tackle rate 27.6%. Late-round/UDFA projection due to limited FBS sample and modest pro day testing (4.59/37.5"/6.96 3-cone). Zero drops in 2025 season.
